text.p: VIENNA July 10 (Reuter) The main stories in the Austrian press this Thursday are:
DER STANDARD
- The pace of the economy's growth has speeded up, a survey of Austrian industry finds.
- Economics Minister Hannes Farnleitner has largely finished drawing up his embattled legislation of the energy sector, which will include the liberalisation of the electricity sector.
- The Steyr group will from early 1998 fully own Steyr-Daimler-Puch Fahrzeugtechnik, which means it will buy back the 50 percent stake in the auto parts maker from Creditanstalt.
DIE PRESSE
- Conservative People's Party leader Wolfgang Schuessel backtracks on the question of NATO membership, saying "give the NATO issue time".
- Tourism in the cities, especially in the east of Austria, is seeing the best growth rates in a long time.
- Raiffeisen Zentralbank is moving into the private banking business in eastern Europe.
- Wuestenrot is interested in buying postal savings bank P.S.K.
- The Bank Austria/Creditanstalt group appears to have had a very profitable first half of the year, with earnings in part getting a boost from international capital markets.
- The number of gasoline service stations is showing a significant decline in Austria. For 1997 alone experts estimate another 200 stations will be closed down.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- The problem child of the Steyr-Daimler-Puch group, Steyr Antriebstechnik, said it will turn in better results this year and is poised for an order boom.
SALZBURGER NACHRICHTEN
- Chancellor Viktor Klima and Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel appeal to the Austrian media not to rush them into a decision over Austrian entry to NATO.
- The Central and Eastern European Economic Summit has opened in Salzburg in a mood of new optimism, according to World Economic Forum president Klaus Schwab.
- First Lady Hilary Rodhmam Clinton is due to arrive in Austria on Friday to speak at a Women's Conference. She will spend four days in Vienna and four in Salzburg.
- Bausparkasse Wuestenrot and Bawag are together eyeing a purchase of PSK.
KURIER
- Johann Berger, father of Formula One racing driver Gerhard Berger, died after he crashed his light aircraft in fog.

- Austria's current account deficit will likely be revised downwards from an initial forecast of a deficit of 40 billion schillings to around 50 billion. Last year's deficit was 40 billion schillings.
